'''Pokhozhaev's identity''' is an integral relation satisfied by stationary [[soliton|localized solutions]] to a [[nonlinear Schrödinger equation]] or [[nonlinear Klein&ndash;Gordon equation]]. It was obtained by [[:ru:%D0%9F%D0%BE%D1%85%D0%BE%D0%B6%D0%B0%D0%B5%D0%B2,_%D0%A1%D1%82%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%81%D0%BB%D0%B0%D0%B2_%D0%98%D0%B2%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87|S.I. Pokhozhaev]]<ref>{{cite journal
|author=Pokhozhaev, S.I.
|title=On the eigenfunctions of the equation <math>\Delta u+\lambda f(u)=0</math>
|journal=Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR
|volume=165
|pages=36&ndash;39
|year=1965
|url=http://mi.mathnet.ru/rus/dan/v165/i1/p36
}}</ref> and is similar to the [[virial theorem]]. This relation is also known as [[Derrick's theorem|G.H. Derrick's theorem]]. Similar identities can be derived for other equations of mathematical physics.

==The Pokhozhaev identity for the stationary nonlinear Schrödinger equation==

Here is a general form due to [[Henri Berestycki|H. Berestycki]] and [[Pierre-Louis Lions|P.-L. Lions]].<ref>{{ cite journal
|author=Berestycki, H. and Lions, P.-L.
|title=Nonlinear scalar field equations, I. Existence of a ground state
|journal=Arch. Rational Mech. Anal.
|volume=82
|issue=4
|year=1983
|pages=313&ndash;345
|doi=10.1007/BF00250555
|bibcode=1983ArRMA..82..313B
|s2cid=123081616
}}</ref>

Let <math>g(s)</math> be continuous and real-valued, with <math>g(0)=0</math>.
Denote <math>G(s)=\int_0^s g(t)\,dt</math>.
Let
:<math>u\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^n),
\qquad
\nabla u\in L^2(\R^n),
\qquad
G(u)\in L^1(\R^n),
\qquad
n\in\N,
</math>
be a solution to the equation
:<math>-\nabla^2 u=g(u)</math>,
[[Distribution (mathematics)|in the sense of distributions]]. 
Then <math>u</math> satisfies the relation
:<math>\frac{n-2}{2}\int_{\R^n}|\nabla u(x)|^2\,dx=n\int_{\R^n}G(u(x))\,dx.</math>

==The Pokhozhaev identity for the stationary nonlinear Dirac equation==

There is a form of the virial identity for the stationary [[nonlinear Dirac equation]] in three spatial dimensions (and also the [[Maxwell-Dirac equations]])<ref>{{ cite journal
|author=Esteban, M. and Séré, E.
|title=Stationary states of the nonlinear Dirac equation: A variational approach
|journal=Commun. Math. Phys.
|volume=171
|issue=2
|year=1995
|pages=323&ndash;350
|doi=10.1007/BF02099273
|bibcode=1995CMaPh.171..323E
|s2cid=120901245
|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1104273565
}}</ref> and in arbitrary spatial dimension.<ref>{{ cite book
|author=Boussaid, N. and Comech, A.
|title=Nonlinear Dirac equation. Spectral stability of solitary waves
|publisher=American Mathematical Society
|series=Mathematical Surveys and Monographs
|volume=244
|year=2019
|doi=10.1090/surv/244
|isbn=978-1-4704-4395-5
|s2cid=216380644
}}</ref>
Let <math>n\in\N,\,N\in\N</math>
and let <math>\alpha^i,\,1\le i\le n</math> and <math>\beta</math> be the [[self-adjoint]] [[Dirac matrices]] of size <math>N\times N</math>:
:<math>
\alpha^i\alpha^j+\alpha^j\alpha^i=2\delta_{ij}I_N,
\quad
\beta^2=I_N,
\quad
\alpha^i\beta+\beta\alpha^i=0,
\quad
1\le i,j\le n.
</math>
Let <math>D_0=-\mathrm{i}\alpha\cdot\nabla=-\mathrm{i}\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha^i\frac{\partial}{\partial x^i}</math> be the massless [[Dirac operator]].
Let <math>g(s)</math> be continuous and real-valued, with <math>g(0)=0</math>.
Denote <math>G(s)=\int_0^s g(t)\,dt</math>.
Let <math>\phi\in L^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(\R^n,\C^N)</math> be a [[spinor]]-valued solution that satisfies the stationary form of the [[nonlinear Dirac equation]],
:<math>
\omega\phi=D_0\phi+g(\phi^\ast\beta\phi)\beta\phi,
</math>
[[Distribution_(mathematics)|in the sense of distributions]],
with some <math>\omega\in\R</math>.
Assume that
:<math>
\phi\in H^1(\R^n,\C^N),\qquad
G(\phi^\ast\beta\phi)\in L^1(\R^n).
</math>
Then <math>\phi</math> satisfies the relation
:<math>
\omega\int_{\R^n}\phi(x)^\ast\phi(x)\,dx
=\frac{n-1}{n}\int_{\R^n}\phi(x)^\ast D_0\phi(x)\,dx
+\int_{\R^n}G(\phi(x)^\ast\beta\phi(x))\,dx.
</math>
